content: 1. In 2018, the World Health Organization (WHO) published a handbook titled Monitoring the Building Blocks of Health Systems, which provides a comprehensive set of indicators and strategies for measuring health system performance. This document is essential for evaluating the effectiveness of health systems globally. 2. The WHO's Consolidated Guidelines on the Use of Antiretroviral Drugs for Treating and Preventing HIV Infection (second edition) outlines evidence-based recommendations for a public health approach to managing HIV. These guidelines emphasize the importance of antiretroviral therapy in both treatment and prevention. 3. The 2017 update of the Guidelines for Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis and Patient Care provides detailed recommendations for managing tuberculosis, focusing on evidence-based practices to improve patient outcomes. 4. The WHO guideline on health policy and system support for optimizing community health worker programs highlights strategies to enhance the effectiveness of community health workers in delivering essential health services. 5. The National eHealth Strategy Toolkit serves as a resource for countries to develop and implement eHealth strategies, ensuring the integration of digital health technologies into national health systems. 6. The Digital Health Atlas is an online platform designed to support the implementation and scale-up of digital health interventions by providing a repository of tools and resources. 7. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and WHO's Be He@lthy, Be Mobile initiative focuses on leveraging mobile technology to promote health and prevent non-communicable diseases. 8. WHO has developed standards and tools to strengthen country-level monitoring and evaluation systems, ensuring the collection and use of high-quality health data for decision-making. 9. The Health Information Systems Interoperability Maturity Toolkit by MEASURE Evaluation provides a framework for assessing and improving the interoperability of health information systems. 10. The WHO guideline on digital interventions for health system strengthening provides evidence-based recommendations for using digital technologies to address health system challenges, such as improving data access and service delivery. 11. The Partnership for Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health has developed a planning workbook for integrating information and communication technologies into health programs for women and children. 12. The Global Digital Health Index is a tool for assessing the maturity and effectiveness of digital health initiatives in different countries. 13. The ITU's Digital Health Platform Handbook provides guidance on building digital information infrastructures for health, emphasizing the importance of interoperability and scalability. 14. The Principles for Digital Development outline best practices for designing and implementing digital health solutions, ensuring they are user-centered and sustainable. 15. The Principles of Donor Alignment for Digital Health emphasize the need for coordinated efforts among donors to support the development of effective digital health systems. 16. The Integrating the Healthcare Enterprise (IHE) initiative provides resources for improving the interoperability of health information systems, facilitating better data exchange and collaboration. 17. The African Alliance and other regional networks promote the use of digital health technologies to address health challenges in low-resource settings. 18. The WeAreAeHIN initiative supports the development of eHealth and health information systems in Asia, fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing. 19. The Global Digital Health Network is a community of practice that brings together stakeholders to share experiences and best practices in digital health. 20. The Health Data Collaborative focuses on improving the availability and use of health data for sustainable development, emphasizing the importance of data quality and interoperability. 21. The WHO's Handbook for Guideline Development provides a systematic approach to developing evidence-based health guidelines, ensuring their relevance and applicability. 22. The Health Information for All initiative aims to improve access to reliable health information, particularly in low-resource settings. 23. The Implementing Best Practices (IBP) Consortium supports the dissemination and implementation of evidence-based practices in global health. 24. The WHO's work on civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) highlights the importance of accurate and timely data for health planning and monitoring. 25. The eRegistries initiative promotes the use of electronic registries for maternal and child health, improving data collection and service delivery. 26. The ICT Facts and Figures report by the ITU provides insights into the global state of information and communication technologies, including their impact on health. 27. The Cochrane Effective Practice and Organisation of Care (EPOC) group provides resources for conducting systematic reviews of health interventions, ensuring the use of high-quality evidence. 28. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement provides guidelines for reporting systematic reviews, enhancing their transparency and reproducibility. 29. The GRADE-CERQual approach helps assess the confidence in findings from qualitative evidence syntheses, supporting evidence-based decision-making in health and social interventions. 30. The WHO's Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 outlines a vision for strengthening the health workforce to achieve universal health coverage. 31. The Introduction to HL7 Standards provides an overview of health data exchange standards, facilitating interoperability in health information systems. 32. The WHO's work on the classification of diseases (ICD) supports the standardization of health data, enabling better tracking of health trends and outcomes. 33. The RE-AIM framework provides a systematic approach to evaluating the impact of health interventions, focusing on their reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance. 34. The Lives Saved Tool is a modeling tool for estimating the impact of health interventions on maternal and child mortality. 35. The iCAT_SR tool helps assess the complexity of interventions within systematic reviews, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of their effectiveness. 36. The WHO and PATH's Planning and Costing Guide for Digital Interventions provides practical guidance for implementing digital health programs, emphasizing cost-effectiveness and sustainability. 37. The WHO's Universal Truth: No Health Without a Workforce report highlights the critical role of health workers in achieving health goals, particularly in underserved areas. 38. The WHO's Telemedicine Opportunities and Developments report provides insights into the use of telemedicine in member states, highlighting its potential to improve access to care. 39. The Effectiveness of Computerized Decision Support Systems review examines the impact of these systems on clinical practice, identifying features critical to their success. 40. The Mobile Learning for Health Professional Education protocol explores the use of mobile technologies for delivering education to health professionals, enhancing their knowledge and skills.
